Jwt.//: DEVELOPMENT KEY. Move to user-secrets or an environment variable before deploying — anyone holding it can mint tokens for any user.

Email.//: Password is NOT here — it lives in user-secrets. Run: dotnet user-secrets set "Email:Password" "<gmail app password>". Until it is set, reset emails are written to the API console instead of being sent.

SupportAi.//: The AI half of the support chatbot. ApiKey is NOT here — it bills to a real Anthropic account, so it lives in user-secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "SupportAi:ApiKey" "sk-ant-...". Until it is set the bot answers from its scripted FAQ only and hands anything else to a human, which is a working product rather than a broken one.

GoogleAuth.//: Sign in with Google. Empty ClientIds means the feature is off and the app hides the button. Create the clients at console.cloud.google.com > APIs and Services > Credentials: one Android client (needs the SHA-1 from `cd android && gradlew signingReport`) and one Web client. Put BOTH ids in the array — the token arrives carrying whichever client signed the user in. The Web client id also goes into the app as GOOGLE_SERVER_CLIENT_ID.

Payments.//: SANDBOX. eSewa's values below are its own published test credentials and are worth nothing. Before going live: set Esewa:MerchantCode and Esewa:SecretKey to your merchant values, drop the 'rc-'/'rc.' from the two eSewa URLs, set Khalti:SecretKey, and change Khalti:BaseUrl to https://khalti.com/api/v2. Put the real secrets in user-secrets or environment variables — never in this file.
Payments.//CallbackBaseUrl: Where the wallet sends the customer back to. Must be reachable from the customer's PHONE, so on a real device this is your LAN address (http://192.168.1.97:5100), not localhost.

Khalti.//: Khalti issues a key per merchant, including sandbox ones — there is no shared test key to ship. Sign up at dev.khalti.com and paste the test secret here (or in user-secrets) to switch the Khalti button on. Until then the app offers eSewa only.
